title: Quantitative soundness of the degree test
statement:
Fix $d \ge 1$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function that is $\varepsilon$-far from degree $\le d$; that is, $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ and every Boolean function $g$ of degree $\le d$ satisfies $\dist(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$. Then the $(d{+}1)$-fold derivative test accepts $f$ with probability at most $1 - \varepsilon$:
\[
  \E_{x}\,\E_{h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}}
  \bigl[\mathbf{1}[\mathrm{GP}((-1)^f, d{+}1, x, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}) = 1]\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \varepsilon,
\]
where $x$ and the direction vectors $h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}$ range uniformly over $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is ε-far from degree ≤ d (which includes 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 and dist(f,g) ≥ ε for all degree ≤ d functions g)
replaced:
If $d \ge 1$ and $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from every degree-$\le d$ function, then
$\Pr[\text{degree test accepts } f] \le 1 - \varepsilon$.
